title: TypeScript Type-Level Programming: Template Literals, Mapped & Conditional Types
summary: Quick revision notes on TypeScript's type-level string and transformation tools: template literal types, Uppercase/Capitalize intrinsics, mapped types with key remapping via `as`, and conditional types with `infer`. Covers the mental model, core usage, common mistakes and a closing cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Type-Level Programming: The Mental Model
points: Types are computed at compile time only: template literal, mapped and conditional types are erased and produce no runtime code
Template literal type: `${A}${B}` builds string literal types; a union in a slot distributes into a union of every combination
Mapped type: `{ [K in Keys]: T }` loops over a union of keys to build an object type, like a for-each over keys
Conditional type: `T extends U ? X : Y` is a type-level if/else, and it distributes over a naked union T
`infer R` declares a type variable inside the `extends` clause of a conditional type and captures whatever matches that position

chapters.title: Template Literal Types and String Intrinsics
points: `type Evt = `on${'click'|'hover'}`` gives `'onclick'|'onhover'`; two unions of sizes m and n produce m×n members
Intrinsic types: Uppercase<S>, Lowercase<S>, Capitalize<S>, Uncapitalize<S> transform string literal types only
Combine: `on${Capitalize<'click'>}` gives `'onClick'`, the standard way to build handler names
Constrain with a pattern: `type Px = `${number}px``, `type Id = `user_${string}`` accept any matching string, and `'12px'` is assignable
Template literals work in pattern position of `extends`, so `S extends `${infer H}${infer T}`` splits strings: H gets exactly the first character, T gets the rest

chapters.title: Mapped Types and Key Remapping with as
points: Basic form: `type Copy<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] }`; homomorphic mapped types (over keyof T) preserve optional and readonly modifiers
Modifiers: `+readonly`/`-readonly` and `+?`/`-?` add or remove them, so `-?` is how Required<T> is built
Key remapping: `[K in keyof T as NewKey]: T[K]` renames each key using the `as` clause
Rename keys with template literals: `[K in keyof T as `get${Capitalize<K & string>}`]: () => T[K]` builds getter names; `K & string` is needed because keyof can include number and symbol
Filter keys by remapping to `never`: `[K in keyof T as T[K] extends Function ? never : K]` drops those keys

chapters.title: Conditional Types and infer
points: `T extends U ? X : Y` checks assignability, not equality; `string extends string | number` is true
Distribution: for a naked type parameter, `ToArray<string | number>` becomes `string[] | number[]`; wrap in a tuple `[T] extends [U]` to turn it off
`never` as a naked parameter distributes over an empty union and returns `never`; guard with `[T] extends [never]`
Extract return type: `T extends (...a: any[]) => infer R ? R : never` is how ReturnType<T> works

Extract element type: `T extends (infer E)[] ? E : T`; extract Promise value recursively: `T extends Promise<infer U> ? Awaited<U> : T`; several `infer` in one position of covariant slots yield a union, in contravariant slots an intersection

chapters.title: Common Mistakes with Type-Level Features
points: Forgetting `K & string` or `Extract<keyof T, string>` before using a key in a template literal gives the error that symbol cannot be used in a template literal
Unions in template literals multiply: large unions in several slots can hit the 100,000-member union limit or slow the compiler
Expecting `T extends U` to distribute when T is wrapped, such as `T[] extends U`, since only a naked parameter distributes
Putting `as` remapping on non-homomorphic key unions loses modifiers: modifiers are only preserved when mapping over `keyof T`
Overusing deep recursive types: instantiation depth is capped (about 50, and 1000 for tail-recursive conditional types), and the error is 'Type instantiation is excessively deep'

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Template, Mapped and Conditional Types
points: Strings: `${A}${B}` combinations; Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, Uncapitalize; pattern slots `${number}`, `${string}`
Mapped: `{ [K in keyof T]: ... }`; modifiers `-?`, `+readonly`; remap `as `get${Capitalize<K & string>}``; drop key with `as never`
Conditional: `T extends U ? X : Y`; distributes over naked unions; opt out with `[T] extends [U]`
Infer: `T extends (...a: any[]) => infer R ? R : never`; `T extends `${infer H}${infer T}``; `T extends (infer E)[] ? E : never`
Recipes: Getters<T> via remap, OmitByType<T,V> via `as never`, CamelCase<S> via recursive infer on `_`, PickByValue via `as T[K] extends V ? K : never`
